rounds.text: Bluestone Jewellery & Lifestyle Ltd is demonstrating explosive top- and bottom-line expansion, led by a compounded sales growth of 42% over the trailing twelve months [E14] alongside a dramatic 164% jump in compounded profit growth [E15]. This stellar fundamental momentum is further validated by a rules-based screen score of 70 out of 100 [E52], driven by immense year-over-year sales surges of 45% [E53] and net profit spikes of 92% [E55]. Operating efficiency is actively scaling, with quarterly operating margins expanding to 13% in September 2026 compared to 8% in the year-ago quarter [E18], positioning results well above sector medians of 18.2% for sales growth and 20.2% for profit growth [E64, E65]. Market participation recognizes this outperformance through a robust relative-strength rating of 94 against the Nifty 500 [E38], while company debt is actively being paid down from Rs 1,984 Cr to Rs 1,918 Cr [E26]. conceded: [E21, E32, E50].

Bluestone Jewellery & Lifestyle Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is completely disconnected from its underlying profitability, evidenced by a trailing P/E of 111x [E1] that balloons to 209.59x against a sector benchmark of just 25.68x [E6]. This lofty pricing carries zero dividend yield [E4] and assumes an unrealistic 32.5% future earnings growth rate through a reverse DCF, far outpacing the 10.0% base case and yielding a staggering -400.9% margin of safety as intrinsic value sits at a mere Rs 152 per share [E32, E33, E34]. Fundamental returns are remarkably depressed, with an ROE of 0.82% [E9] and ROCE of 6.38% [E10] severely trailing sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10], while working capital bloat has driven working capital days from 85.5 to 132 days [E51] and resulted in negative operating cash flow of Rs -199 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs -276 Cr [E22, E23]. Conceded: compounded sales growth of 42% [E14], profit growth of 164% [E15], and a quarterly operating margin expansion to 13% in Sep 2026 [E18] show genuine top-line and recent operational momentum.

Conceded: trailing P/E of 111x [E1], P/E of 209.59x versus sector [E6], zero dividend yield [E4], intrinsic value at Rs 152 with a -400.9% margin of safety [E32, E33], and a reverse DCF implying 32.5% earnings growth [E34]. However, dismissing this company on static historical returns ignores massive forward momentum where compounded sales growth hits 42% [E14] and compounded profit growth reaches 164% [E15]. Conceded: ROE of 0.82% [E9], ROCE of 6.38% [E10], negative operating cash flow of Rs -199 Cr [E22], free cash flow of Rs -276 Cr [E23], and working capital days rising to 132 days [E51]. Yet the business is actively outperforming expectations through a recent quarterly operating margin expansion to 13% in Sep 2026 from 8% a year ago [E18], supported by expected good quarters [E46]. Conceded: institutional outflow [E60]. Nonetheless, results score an impressive 84/100 with net profit up 92% YoY [E62], proving that a turnaround is already underway and making stale sentiment and lagging historical ratios a poor guide to future potential [E62].

Conceded: compounded sales growth is 42% [E14], compounded profit growth is 164% [E15], quarterly operating margin expanded to 13% against 8% a year ago [E18], and the results score 84/100 with net profit up 92% YoY [E62]. However, this rapid growth has not translated into operational cash generation, as operating cash flow remains deeply negative at Rs -199 Cr and free cash flow sits at Rs -276 Cr [E22, E23]. The bull points to margin expansion, but the yearly operating margin trend is actually inconsistent over the last three years and the quarterly trend has been actively decreasing over the last four quarters [E19, E20]. Furthermore, working capital blockages have worsened with days surging from 85.5 to 132 days [E51], undermining the quality of those headline growth figures.
